html:
On 26 December 1991 the Soviet Union formally ceased to exist, and its fifteen republics became independent states. For Central Asia, it ended more than a century of Russian and Soviet rule.

The causes built up over years: a stagnant economy, the cost of the arms race and the war in Afghanistan, nationalism in the republics, and the reforms of Mikhail Gorbachev, glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring), which loosened control without fixing the economy. In 1989 the communist regimes of Eastern Europe fell, symbolised by the fall of the Berlin Wall.

The final steps:

  • 1988 to 1990: the Baltic republics declared sovereignty, then independence.
  • August 1991: hardliners tried to overthrow Gorbachev in the August coup. It failed within days, and Boris Yeltsin, president of Russia, came out the winner.
  • Autumn 1991: most republics declared independence.
  • 8 December: the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed the Belovezha Accords, declaring the Union dead.
  • 16 December: Kazakhstan was the last republic to declare independence.
  • 21 December: in Alma-Ata, eleven republics joined the new Commonwealth of Independent States.
  • 25 December: Gorbachev resigned; the Soviet flag came down over the Kremlin.

The Central Asian leaders, such as Nursultan Nazarbayev, had mostly wanted to keep a reformed union. They became heads of the independent republics almost by default.
sum: On 26 December 1991 the Soviet Union formally ceased to exist, and its fifteen republics became independent states. For Central Asia, it ended more than a century of Russian and Soviet rule.
